title: Essential-image test on derived maps into simplicial categories
statement:
Use simplicial categories and the Bergner homotopy category $h\mathrm{sCat}$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus]. For a simplicial category $T$, let $\pi_0T$ have the objects of $T$ and the connected components of its mapping simplicial sets as morphisms. Let $j:T\to T'$ be a simplicial functor inducing a weak homotopy equivalence $T(x,y)\to T'(jx,jy)$ for every pair of objects. For every small simplicial category $I$, postcomposition is injective:
$$j_*:\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(I,T)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(I,T').$$
Its image consists exactly of the classes $a$ for which the induced functor $\pi_0I\to\pi_0T'$, defined up to natural isomorphism, has essential image contained in that of $\pi_0j$. Essential image means objects isomorphic to an object in the image. All categories and hom sets fit in a fixed sufficiently large universe. No essential-surjectivity hypothesis on $j$ is assumed.

source.place: Corollary A.3.4.11, printed p.889; maps in the Bergner homotopy category are tested on their induced ordinary homotopy-category functor. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: Work in the Bergner model category of [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property], with the ordinary model-category axioms of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test]. Factor $T'\to *$ as a trivial cofibration $r:T'\to B$ followed by a fibration. Thus $B$ is fibrant and $r$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Put $u=rj:T\to B$. On every mapping simplicial set, $u$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by the hypothesis on $j$, the local weak-equivalence clause for $r$, and two-out-of-three. Let $B_0$ be the full simplicial subcategory of $B$ on the objects isomorphic in $\pi_0B$ to some $u(t)$, and write $i:B_0\hookrightarrow B$. Explicitly, $B_0(b,c)=B(b,c)$ with the inherited units and composition. The map $u$ factors as $iv$ for $v:T\to B_0$. This $v$ is locally a weak equivalence and its component functor is fully faithful and essentially surjective, hence an equivalence: a quasi-inverse chooses an isomorphic image for each object and transports each arrow using full faithfulness. Thus $v$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence and $[v]$ is invertible in $h\mathrm{sCat}$.

proof.text: The inclusion $i$ is a Bergner fibration by the generating-trivial-cofibration lifting criterion of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. Its local maps are identities, hence Kan fibrations. If $b\in B_0$ and a vertex $e:b\to c$ is invertible in $\pi_0B$, then $c\in B_0$ by repleteness. The same vertex $e$ and its inverse component belong to the full subcategory, so $e$ is the required invertible lift, with endpoint exactly $c$. These are both clauses of the cited criterion. Since $B$ is fibrant, composition of fibrations makes $B_0$ fibrant too: right lifting classes are closed under composition by solving two successive lifting problems. The model structure and factorization terminology are those of [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property].

proof.text: Choose a cofibrant replacement $q:A\to I$ by factoring $\varnothing\to I$ as a cofibration followed by a trivial fibration. These model factorizations are provided by [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property] with the axioms of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test]. The representation theorem [lem-coef-model-localization-homotopy-classes], applied in this model category, says that every morphism from $[A]$ to $[B]$ or to $[B_0]$ is represented by an actual enriched functor, since $A$ is cofibrant and both targets are fibrant. As $[q]$ is invertible, a class $a:[I]\to[B]$ is therefore represented by $[f][q]^{-1}$ for an enriched $f:A\to B$. The same holds for classes with target $B_0$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: independent enriched-model foundation for the essential-image restriction. Agent proof of the assertion of HTT Corollary A.3.4.11; HTT archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Prepare a good cylinder for $A$. Factor the fold $A\amalg A\to A$ as a cofibration $(e_0,e_1):A\amalg A\to C$ followed by a trivial fibration $c:C\to A$. Thus $ce_0=ce_1=1_A$. Each inclusion $A\to A\amalg A$ is a pushout of the cofibration $\varnothing\to A$, so both $e_0,e_1$ are cofibrations. Cofibrations are closed under pushout and composition: rewrite a lifting problem over a pushout as the original lifting problem, and solve successive lifting problems for a composite. Since $c$ is weak, two-out-of-three makes $e_0,e_1$ weak too. Hence each endpoint map is a trivial cofibration, and this is a good cylinder in the terminology of [lem-coef-localized-good-homotopy-test]. All factorizations and closure arguments here use the weak factorization systems in [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property] and [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test].

proof.text: To prove injectivity of $i_*$, represent two classes with target $B_0$ by $f,g:A\to B_0$ as in Step 3, and suppose $[if]=[ig]$. Apply [lem-coef-localized-good-homotopy-test] with cofibrant source $A$, fibrant target $B$, and the good cylinder of Step 4. It gives $H:C\to B$ with $He_0=if$ and $He_1=ig$. Since $e_0$ is a trivial cofibration and $i$ a fibration, the model lifting axiom supplies $\widetilde H:C\to B_0$ with $\widetilde He_0=f$ and $i\widetilde H=H$. At the other endpoint, $i\widetilde He_1=ig$. Inclusion of a full subcategory is injective on objects and identical on the retained mapping sets, so $\widetilde He_1=g$ as enriched functors. Thus this same good cylinder gives a left homotopy between $f,g$ in $B_0$, and the cited test yields $[f]=[g]$. Precomposing with $[q]^{-1}$ proves injectivity on maps from $I$. The lift uses precisely the trivial-cofibration/fibration weak factorization system of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test].

proof.text: For the image assertion first use target $B$. The component-category construction sends a Dwyer--Kan equivalence to an equivalence of ordinary categories. Thus a derived map represented as $[f][q]^{-1}$ has component functor represented by $\pi_0 f$ after identifying $\pi_0 A$ with $\pi_0I$ via $\pi_0q$; this is the induced-functor convention in [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. The essential-image condition is therefore equivalent to every $f(x)$, $x\in A$, being isomorphic in $\pi_0 B$ to some $u(t)$. Indeed every object of $\pi_0I$ is isomorphic to an image under $\pi_0q$, and functors preserve these isomorphisms. By the definition of $B_0$ this says exactly that each $f(x)$ is an object of $B_0$. In that event $f$ factors literally through $B_0$: retain its object function and its action on mapping sets, which have the same source and target sets in the full subcategory. Consequently $[f][q]^{-1}$ is in the image of $i_*$. Conversely each class in that image is represented by $ig$ with $g:A\to B_0$ by Step 3, so every object value satisfies the required condition. This proves both directions without selecting incoherent lifts of arrows.

source.place: Paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: independent enriched-model foundation for the essential-image restriction. Agent proof of the assertion of HTT Corollary A.3.4.11; HTT archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Since $u=iv$ with $[v]$ invertible by Step 1, the injectivity and image criterion of Steps 5--6 give the assertion for $u:T\to B$. Finally $u=rj$ and $[r]$ is invertible. Postcomposition with $[r]$ identifies the maps into $T'$ with those into $B$. Under this identification the induced component functors are carried along the equivalence $\pi_0r$. An equivalence preserves and reflects membership in an essential image: if $r(y)$ is isomorphic to $rj(t)$, full faithfulness lifts this isomorphism and its inverse to $y\cong j(t)$; preservation is immediate. Thus the criterion in $B$ is exactly the stated criterion in $T'$, and injectivity also transfers across this bijection. Inverting the weak equivalences is the homotopy-category convention of [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property].

proof.text: Use the functorial object-preserving replacements T→RT and T′→RT′ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Naturality gives the commuting square of mapping simplicial sets with horizontal maps T(x,y)→T′(jx,jy) and RT(x,y)→RT′(jx,jy). The vertical maps and the top map are weak homotopy equivalences, so two-out-of-three makes the bottom map a weak homotopy equivalence. Put X=N_hc(RT), Y=N_hc(RT′), and J=N_hc(Rj). The natural mapping-space comparisons in that node identify the bottom map with Map_X(x,y)→Map_Y(Jx,Jy). Thus J is fully faithful. Put A=N_hc(RI); no cofibrancy assumption on I is needed.

proof.text: Let Y₀ be the full subcategory of Y on the objects equivalent to Jx for some x∈X, and let i:Y₀→Y be the inclusion. By [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image], J factors as iJ₀ and J₀:X→Y₀ admits a coherent quasi-inverse K:Y₀→X, with coherent natural equivalences KJ₀≃1_X and J₀K≃1_Y₀. Its hypotheses hold because Step 1 proves full faithfulness and Y₀ is exactly the full replete essential image specified in that node.

proof.text: The derived coherent-nerve equivalence in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] identifies Hom_{h sCat}(I,T) with coherent functors A→X modulo coherent natural equivalence, and identifies Hom_{h sCat}(I,T′) with coherent functors A→Y modulo coherent natural equivalence. These are the morphisms in the ordinary homotopy category of Cat_∞. Naturality identifies j_* with postcomposition by J. All objects and functor categories are taken in the sufficiently large universe of the statement. It therefore remains to check injectivity and the image criterion for these functors.

proof.text: By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], a full subcategory contains precisely all simplices with its specified vertices. Thus a simplicial map a:A→Y whose vertices lie in Y₀ factors literally as ia₀ with a₀:A→Y₀. Moreover an equivalence between iJ₀F and iJ₀G in Fun(A,Y) factors into Fun(A,Y₀): its transformation, its inverse, and the two inverse-triangle witnesses have all vertices among the values of J₀F and J₀G. (For a chain of such equivalences the same argument applies, since Y₀ is replete.) Applying K and whiskering KJ₀≃1_X from Step 2 yields F≃KJ₀F≃KJ₀G≃G, proving injectivity. For a functor a=ia₀ as above, put b=Ka₀. Whiskering J₀K≃1_Y₀ gives Jb=iJ₀Ka₀≃ia₀=a. Conversely every Jb has all vertices in Y₀. This proves that the image consists precisely of functors whose vertex values lie in Y₀, without choosing separate, potentially incompatible lifts of their arrows.

proof.text: The object-preserving replacement and mapping-space comparison in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] identify π₀T with the ordinary homotopy category of X, and π₀T′ with that of Y, naturally for j; the same applies to I and A. Composition agrees because the comparison preserves enriched composition. An object y of Y lies in Y₀ exactly when y and Jx are isomorphic in its homotopy category for some x. Here the homotopy category of the quasicategory Y has as morphisms the components of the right-pinched mapping spaces Map_Y(y,y′) of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], that is, homotopy classes of edges, and a 2-simplex with edges f:y→y′, g:y′→y″ and long edge h says [h]=[g][f]. If f:y→Jx is an equivalence in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], its inverse g and the two triangle witnesses (2-simplices with edges (f,g,1_y) and (g,f,1_{Jx})) give [g][f]=[1_y] and [f][g]=[1_{Jx}]. Conversely let [f],[g] be inverse classes. Fill the inner horn Λ²₁ given by (f,g) to a 2-simplex σ with long edge h. Then [h]=[1_y], so h and 1_y lie in one component of the Kan complex Map_Y(y,y) and are joined by an edge (in either direction, the space being Kan). Such an edge is a homotopy between h and 1_y, and by the equivalence of the two forms of homotopy (Scholze, basic fact (2)) it gives a 2-simplex τ with edges h, 1_y and long edge 1_y. The inner horn Λ³₂ on vertices y,Jx,y,y with faces d₃=σ, d₁=τ and d₀ the degenerate 2-simplex on g fills in Y, and its face d₂ is a 2-simplex with edges (f,g,1_y). The other witness is obtained in the same way from [f][g]=[1_{Jx}]. This is Scholze's basic fact (3) of Lecture II. Thus the vertex condition of Step 4 is exactly the stated essential-image condition on π₀a. Equivalent coherent functors induce naturally isomorphic homotopy-category functors, by taking the components and naturality triangles of the coherent equivalence; hence this condition is independent of the representative of a. Combining Steps 3-4 proves both clauses, without essential surjectivity of j.
